title: Flight checkout UI and flow
idea: The flight booking frontend is a results list, a passenger form and a payment step driven by one reducer, with an Idempotency-Key made before each request.
points: `BookingPage` owns the reducer; `PassengerForm` calls the API client and dispatches results.
Keys are made when a step starts, so retries and double submits reuse them.
A 409 sold out sends the user back to results with a clear message.
Follow-ups: cache search results, add round trips, push live seat counts.

messages.note: The response is lost. The UI cannot tell whether the hold happened.

messages.label: retry with hk-2
messages.note: The retry reuses the same key, so the server finds the stored booking.

messages.label: 200 PNR-4 HELD
messages.note: Same PNR, no second hold. The reducer moves to PAYING with a fresh payment key.

messages.label: POST /bookings/PNR-4/payment
messages.note: Payment carries its own key, so a retried charge is applied once.

messages.label: 200 TICKETED
messages.note: The confirmation screen shows the PNR and ticket numbers.

code.title: Checkout reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then add a second PAY_CLICKED after the first and predict the output.

walk.text: The whole screen state: step, fare, passengers, PNR, two keys and an error.
Selecting a fare starts a hold attempt; the event carries its new key.
Invalid names show an error; a submit outside PASSENGERS is ignored.
A failure keeps the key for the retry; sold out resets to results.
A held booking gets its payment key; pay is ignored unless PAYING.
Hold expiry resets the screen, unless payment is in flight or tickets are issued.
Replay the events and print step, keys and error after each one.

code.title: PassengerForm component
code.caption: A React component that renders state, calls the API and dispatches events. Not run here.

walk.text: Local state holds only the form fields, one entry per passenger.
Guard the step, validate names, then move the reducer to HOLDING.
Call the API with the existing key; map each outcome to an event, making the payment key.
Errors render in an alert region so screen readers announce them.
The button is disabled outside PASSENGERS, so a held fare cannot be resubmitted.

pitfalls: Do not make a new key on every click; make it once when the step starts.
Disabling a button is not enough; a fast double submit still needs the same key.
Show the server's `holdUntil` as the countdown; device clocks drift.

quiz.q: In the run, what is holdKey after the second SELECT_FARE?
quiz.why: The sold-out reset cleared hk-1. Selecting Y-FLEX starts a new hold attempt, so SELECT_FARE makes the next key, hk-2.

takeaway: One reducer owns the screen; keys made early make retries safe.

starters: Why make the Idempotency-Key when the fare is selected?
How would a round-trip booking change this reducer?
